steps.label: ER and HER2 Receptor Heterogeneity
quotes: [PMID:27349894] [SUPPORT] Intratumoral biomarker heterogeneity may impact breast cancer classification accuracy, with implications for clinical management. --- Explanation: This supports clinically meaningful intratumoral ER/PR/HER2 heterogeneity within primary breast cancers, affecting biomarker-based classification and treatment selection.

steps.label: TP53 Loss of Function
quotes: [PMID:23000897] [SUPPORT] Somatic mutations in only three genes (TP53, PIK3CA and GATA3) occurred at >10% incidence across all breast cancers --- Explanation: Places somatic TP53 mutation among the three lesions recurring across all breast cancers in the TCGA cohort, which is what makes it a shared-biology node of the base entry rather than content belonging to one stratum.|[PMID:21336307] [SUPPORT] loss of p53 correlates with a decrease in the level of miR-200c, but an increase in the expression of EMT and stemness markers, and development of a high tumour grade in a cohort of breast tumours --- Explanation: Human breast tumour cohort in which loss of p53 tracks with loss of its target miR-200c and with expression of EMT markers, supporting the loss of p53 transcriptional output in patient tumours.

steps.label: EMT-Driven Dissemination
quotes: [PMID:21336307] [SUPPORT] Loss of p53 in mammary epithelial cells leads to decreased expression of miR-200c and activates the EMT programme, accompanied by an increased mammary stem cell population. --- Explanation: States the causal step this edge asserts: removing p53 from mammary epithelial cells activates the EMT programme, through loss of miR-200c.

steps.label: PIK3CA Oncogenic Mutations
quotes: [DOI:10.1158/2159-8290.cd-23-0944] [SUPPORT] PIK3CA (PI3Kα) is a lipid kinase commonly mutated in cancer, including ∼40% of hormone receptor–positive breast cancer. The most frequently observed mutants occur in the kinase and helical domains. --- Explanation: Establishes hotspot helical and kinase domain PIK3CA mutations as the recurrent activating lesions in HR+ breast cancer.|[PMID:15647370] [SUPPORT] Expressed in chicken embryo fibroblasts, all three mutants induce oncogenic transformation with high efficiency. This transforming ability is correlated with elevated catalytic activity in in vitro kinase assays. --- Explanation: Grounds the gene and molecular-function bindings on this node. The three hotspot mutants the description names (E542K, E545K, H1047R) raise the catalytic activity of the PIK3CA-encoded enzyme itself in kinase assays, which is the gain-of-function claim, as distinct from the downstream pathway readouts cited on the nodes below.

steps.label: Endocrine Resistance
quotes: [DOI:10.1186/s13058-023-01718-0] [SUPPORT] ESR1 and PIK3CA codon variants, together with alterations in specific oncogenic pathways, can differentially impact the biology and clinical phenotype of luminal-like MBC. --- Explanation: ctDNA analysis demonstrates ESR1/PIK3CA crosstalk shapes luminal-like metastatic breast cancer biology, supporting endocrine resistance via PI3K-ER pathway interplay.

steps.label: Cell Survival and Proliferation
quotes: [DOI:10.1158/2159-8290.cd-23-0944] [SUPPORT] RLY-2608 inhibited tumor growth in PIK3CA-mutant xenograft models with minimal impact on insulin --- Explanation: Mutant-selective PI3Kα inhibition reduces PIK3CA-mutant tumor growth, consistent with the proliferative dependency on PI3K-AKT signaling.

drug_evidence.name: Palbociclib
quotes: [DOI:10.1007/s10549-024-07376-w] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] Patients receiving 1st-line aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor (n = 573) with ESR1mut had less favorable rwPFS and rwOS versus ESR1 wild-type; no differences were observed for fulvestrant + CDK4/6 inhibitor (n = 348). --- Explanation: Real-world metastatic HR+/HER2- cohorts document aromatase-inhibitor and fulvestrant backbones paired with CDK4/6 inhibitors in first-line therapy.|[PMID:41744884] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] for HR+/HER2- mBC, first-line endocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitor, followed by targeted agents, chemotherapy, or antibody-drug conjugates based on progression and visceral crisis --- Explanation: The Romanian consensus statement recommends first-line endocrine therapy plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor for HR-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer.

drug_evidence.name: Fulvestrant
quotes: [DOI:10.1007/s10549-024-07376-w] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] Patients receiving 1st-line aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor (n = 573) with ESR1mut had less favorable rwPFS and rwOS versus ESR1 wild-type; no differences were observed for fulvestrant + CDK4/6 inhibitor (n = 348). --- Explanation: Real-world metastatic HR+/HER2- cohorts document aromatase-inhibitor and fulvestrant backbones paired with CDK4/6 inhibitors in first-line therapy.|[PMID:41744884] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] for HR+/HER2- mBC, first-line endocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitor, followed by targeted agents, chemotherapy, or antibody-drug conjugates based on progression and visceral crisis --- Explanation: The Romanian consensus statement recommends first-line endocrine therapy plus a CDK4/6 inhibitor for HR-positive/HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer.

drug_evidence.name: Elacestrant
quotes: [DOI:10.1200/jco.23.02112] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved elacestrant for the treatment of postmenopausal women or adult men with estrogen receptor–positive (ER+), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2–negative (HER2–), estrogen receptor 1 ( ESR1)–mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer with disease progression after at least one line of endocrine therapy (ET). --- Explanation: FDA approval summary supports elacestrant for ESR1-mutated ER+/HER2- advanced or metastatic breast cancer after endocrine therapy.

drug_evidence.name: capivasertib
quotes: [clinicaltrials:NCT04305496] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] Phase III, double-blind, randomised study assessing the efficacy of capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant for the treatment of patients with locally advanced (inoperable) or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer following recurrence or progression on or after AI therapy. --- Explanation: CAPItello-291 directly evaluates capivasertib plus fulvestrant in locally advanced or metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer after aromatase-inhibitor progression.

drug_evidence.name: Olaparib
quotes: [DOI:10.1038/s41416-024-02827-z] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] BC resulting from a germline BRCAm (gBRCAm) has distinct clinical characteristics along with increased sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents such as poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors and platinum-based chemotherapies, and potentially decreased sensitivity to cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors. --- Explanation: Review-level evidence supports PARP inhibitor sensitivity in germline BRCA-mutated breast cancer, including advanced-disease treatment planning.

drug_evidence.name: Talazoparib
quotes: [DOI:10.1038/s41416-024-02827-z] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] BC resulting from a germline BRCAm (gBRCAm) has distinct clinical characteristics along with increased sensitivity to DNA-damaging agents such as poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors and platinum-based chemotherapies, and potentially decreased sensitivity to cyclin-dependent kinase 4 and 6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors. --- Explanation: Review-level evidence supports PARP inhibitor sensitivity in germline BRCA-mutated breast cancer, including advanced-disease treatment planning.

drug_evidence.name: Trastuzumab deruxtecan
quotes: [DOI:10.3390/cancers17213505] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] Trastuzumab–deruxtecan (T-DXd), a new-generation antibody drug conjugate, has greatly improved the survival and clinical benefit rates of patients affected by advanced HER2-positive/HER2-low breast cancer according to the results of controlled clinical trials with a manageable safety profile. --- Explanation: This review summarizes T-DXd benefit for advanced HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancer.

drug_evidence.name: Sacituzumab govitecan
quotes: [clinicaltrials:NCT04639986] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] The goal of this study is to compare the study drug, sacituzumab govitecan-hziy, versus doctors' treatment of choice in participants with HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (MBC) who have failed at least 2 prior chemotherapy regimens. --- Explanation: The phase 3 record supports sacituzumab govitecan evaluation in heavily pretreated HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer.

drug_evidence.name: Alpelisib
quotes: [PMID:37743730] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] The combination of fulvestrant with alpelisib, a PI3K inhibitor, improves progression-free survival in metastatic hormone receptor-positive, PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer. --- Explanation: This abstract supports the use of alpelisib with fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutant breast cancer.

drug_evidence.name: inavolisib
quotes: [clinicaltrials:NCT04191499] [INDIRECT EVIDENCE] [SUPPORT] This study will evaluate the efficacy, safety, and pharmacokinetics of inavolisib in combination with palbociclib and fulvestrant compared with placebo plus palbociclib and fulvestrant in participants with PIK3CA-mutant, hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer --- Explanation: ClinicalTrials.gov record for INAVO120 confirms that the studied regimen combines inavolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
